name: Respiratory variants & flu
value: Early US flu season; no system strain found
summary: US flu admissions at their highest for the time of year since 2010–11; UK flu above baseline but low impact
state: CDC data for the week to 24 Oct showed 6,100 flu admissions, an estimated rate the highest for that week since 2010–11, with forecasts of further rises to mid-November (Nature World News, 4 Nov). UKHSA's report of 5 Nov, updated 12 Nov, shows flu admissions of 2.83 per 100,000, up from 2.51 but in the low-impact range, with activity above baseline (UKHSA). Searches on 15 Nov found no new WHO variant designation and no health systems reported as strained, so an unusually early US season keeps this at Watch.
for_you: Older people, young children, pregnant women and people with long-term conditions are most exposed. In the UK, the NHS and UKHSA advise eligible people to get their flu and COVID-19 vaccines.
rubric_hit: Watch: a hemisphere's flu season unusually early (US admissions highest for the week since 2010–11); no variant of concern

sources.title: Nature World News — CDC forecasts flu hospitalizations will likely keep climbing through mid-November
UKHSA — National flu and COVID-19 surveillance report: 5 November 2026 (week 45)

why: Known viruses change; a new COVID-19 variant or a severe flu strain can strain health systems without being 'novel'.
drivers: Viral evolution, waning immunity, seasonal patterns, vaccine match.

rubric.alert: WHO designates a variant of concern, or flu or COVID-19 hospitalisations strain several countries' health systems.
rubric.watch: WHO designates a new variant of interest, or a hemisphere's flu season is unusually early or severe.
rubric.normal: No WHO variant of interest rising fast; flu seasons of normal severity.
